q: Roatán, the largest of Honduras's Bay Islands, sits on which huge coral reef, the second-largest barrier reef in the world?
explain: The Mesoamerican Barrier Reef runs along the Caribbean coasts of Mexico, Belize, Guatemala and Honduras.

q: What is the largest natural lake in Honduras, a freshwater lake set in the western highlands?
explain: Lake Yojoa is the largest natural lake in Honduras and a favourite spot for boating and birdwatching.

q: Which volcano in El Salvador, born in 1770, erupted so often that sailors called it the 'Lighthouse of the Pacific'?
explain: Izalco glowed with near-constant eruptions for almost 200 years, guiding ships at night. It has been quiet since 1966.

q: Chile is a very long, thin country that runs down the coast of which ocean?
explain: Chile stretches about 4,300 km along South America's Pacific coast, but is rarely more than 200 km wide.

q: The giant stone moai statues of Easter Island were carved by the island's Polynesian people, who are known as what?
explain: The Rapa Nui people of Easter Island, which is part of Chile, carved the famous moai statues over many centuries.

q: What is the highest mountain in Peru, a snow-capped peak in the Andes?
explain: Huascarán, in Peru's Cordillera Blanca, is the country's highest peak and a famous challenge for climbers.

q: The ruined city of Machu Picchu, set high in the Andes of Peru, was built by which civilisation in the 1400s?
explain: Machu Picchu was built by the Inca civilisation around 1450 and is one of the most famous archaeological sites in the world.

q: Which major river forms part of the border between Venezuela and Colombia, then flows east across Venezuela to the Atlantic Ocean?
explain: The Orinoco is Venezuela's great river. It ends in a huge delta on the Atlantic coast.

q: The Catatumbo lightning, one of the world's most constant thunderstorms, flashes almost every night over which Venezuelan lake?
explain: The Catatumbo lightning storms over Lake Maracaibo in Venezuela are among the most constant thunderstorms on Earth.

q: Which famous islands, home to giant tortoises and marine iguanas found nowhere else, belong to Ecuador?
explain: The Galápagos Islands, a province of Ecuador, are famous for their unique wildlife, including giant tortoises and marine iguanas.

q: Ecuador is named after which imaginary line that runs around the middle of the Earth?
explain: Ecuador takes its name from the Equator, the imaginary line of latitude that circles the globe and passes right through the country.

q: Ecuador's capital, Quito, is built on the slopes of which active volcano?
explain: Quito lies on the eastern slopes of Pichincha, high in the Andes. Popocatépetl is in Mexico, Etna in Italy and Fuji in Japan.

q: Bolivia shares the huge, high Lake Titicaca with which neighbouring country?
explain: Lake Titicaca sits high in the Andes on the border between Bolivia and Peru.

q: Bolivia has two capital cities — La Paz is where the government sits, but which city is the official constitutional capital?
explain: Sucre is Bolivia's constitutional capital, while La Paz is the seat of government and the country's largest city.

q: The ancient ruins of Tiwanaku, with their famous Gateway of the Sun, lie near which huge lake high in the Andes?
explain: Tiwanaku was the centre of a great civilisation near the southern shore of Lake Titicaca, long before the Inca.

q: Paraguay is one of only two landlocked countries in South America — which is the other?
explain: Bolivia and Paraguay are the only two landlocked countries in South America.
